final_candidates.decision_summary: R157 is a critical catalytic residue involved in substrate binding and orientation. Alanine substitution disrupts substrate binding and reliably abolishes enzyme activity.
D191 serves as an essential catalytic proton transfer residue. Alanine substitution eliminates catalytic acid/base activity, resulting in severe loss of function.
Charge reversal at active-site position 157 severely destabilizes substrate interaction in the catalytic pocket, causing loss of catalytic competence.

stop_reason.detail: Optimal Top-3 loss-of-function candidates targeting catalytic site residues were verified against the WT sequence and finalized.

history.rationale: Arg157 is a critical catalytic domain residue involved in folate/FAD substrate binding; alanine substitution removes key ionic/hydrogen bonding interactions, abolishing enzyme activity.
R157 is a critical active site residue involved in substrate binding; alanine mutation reliably abolishes enzymatic activity.
Asp191 acts as a catalytic carboxylate required for proton transfer; alanine mutation removes the side-chain carboxyl group and destroys catalytic function.
D191 acts as an essential catalytic acid/base residue; replacing it with alanine results in complete loss of function.
Trp95 forms essential aromatic stacking interactions with the flavin cofactor ring; substitution with alanine impairs FAD binding and abolishes activity.
W95 is critical for FAD cofactor binding via aromatic stacking; substitution with alanine abolishes cofactor retention.
Introduces a charge reversal at essential active site residue Arg157, severely disrupting active site electrostatics and substrate binding.
Charge reversal at catalytic position 157 severely disrupts substrate stabilization and completely impairs catalysis.
Neutralizes the essential catalytic charge of Asp191 while preserving size, specifically preventing required acid-base proton transfer steps.
Eliminating the negative charge at catalytic D191 via asparagine substitution disables essential proton transfer.
His181 is a key active site histidine involved in catalytic proton shuttle machinery; alanine substitution abolishes enzymatic activity.
H181 forms essential active site interactions; alanine mutation disrupts catalytic efficiency.
Glu185 is part of the core catalytic domain loop; charge reversal to lysine severely destabilizes active site architecture.
E185K introduces a bulky positive charge in the active site pocket, severely disrupting function.
Arg134 stabilizes active site loop conformations and substrate positioning; charge reversal abolishes MTHFR activity.
R134 participates in domain-stabilizing salt bridges; charge inversion causes loss of catalytic competence.
Trp339 participates in hydrophobic/aromatic core interactions in the catalytic domain; alanine substitution disrupts domain integrity and activity.
Position 339 in the provided sequence is glycine (G), not tryptophan (W); candidate rejected due to sequence mismatch.

rejection.reason: Position 339 in the provided sequence is glycine (G), not tryptophan (W); candidate rejected due to sequence mismatch.

history.rationale: Gly158 resides in a tight catalytic loop; substitution with bulky charged arginine creates severe steric clash and abolishes catalytic turn geometry.
G158R is a well-established severe loss-of-function pathogenic mutation in human MTHFR.
